design.summary:
The query that was benchmarked is not the state.cljs built-in. Both bench graphs (~/.cache/lsbench/g-10k and g-real) have the same :default-queries block as Johan's own config (~/OneDrive/Logseq/logseq/config.edn:142-172; I diffed them). merge-configs (state.cljs:443-453) replaces the built-in :journals vector with it. That override is the old Logseq 0.10.x template. It uses [?h :block/marker ?marker] plus [(contains? ...)], and [?p :block/journal? true]. Nothing in this codebase writes :block/journal? any more; journal pages get :block/type "journal" (graph-parser block.cljs:360). So Johan's NOW and NEXT always return nothing, and the empty sections are hidden (components/query.cljs:170). Each run still costs 1.6-3.1 s at 10k.

The engine is the reason reordering does not help. The DataScript fork runs clauses strictly in order (query.cljc:817-819). It uses a bound variable as a lookup key only when its relation has exactly one tuple (query.cljc:382-391). Date predicates only filter rows after the lookup (query.cljc:409 is a TODO for exactly this). So every pattern whose variable holds more than one value reads the whole attribute. g-10k has 77 NOW/DOING tasks, so [?h :block/page ?p] reads all ~58 000 :block/page datoms, and that scan most likely dominates. This matches the reviewed note in bench/step3-designs.json.

- **Reordering alone:** does not work. The date pattern still reads all 10 000 journal pages, and ~15 ?p values still read all of :block/page.
- **:db/index on :block/marker:** does not help, and is unsafe for existing graphs without a re-index.
- **Smallest bounded fix:** a fast path in the worker's :thread-api/q. It recognizes this query shape by its clauses and answers it with index walks: d/index-range on :block/journal-day (≤15 datoms), then the AVET :block/page datoms of each page, then an EAVT marker check per block, then pull. Any other query falls back to d/q unchanged.
- **Compat rewrite:** in query_react/resolve-query, turn [?p :block/journal? true] into [?p :block/type "journal"], so old configs like Johan's show results again.

A general query-engine fix is possible but is a large change to the fork: lookups by a small set of bound values, plus pushing date ranges into the index. It fits a later ADR-003 step, not this fix.
design.current_behavior:
RENDER: page.cljs:714-715 mounts today-queries (page.cljs:239-258) only on today's journal. For each entry in (state/sub-config) [:default-queries :journals] it renders query/custom-query with :built-in-query? true and :today-query? true. Then custom-query* (components/query.cljs:133-197) calls query-result/run-custom-query (query/result.cljs:19, 56-58), which calls query-custom/custom-query (query_custom.cljs:69-86). The query is a vector starting with :find, so it is raw datalog, not the query DSL. add-rules-to-query (query_custom.cljs:27-67) finds `task` in :where, appends % to :in and puts the file `task` rule (rules.cljc:30-33) into :rules. Johan's override has no rule call, so it gets no %. Then query-react/react-query (query_react.cljs:95-120) runs.

INPUTS: resolved on the UI thread at query_react.cljs:108 by db-inputs/resolve-input (deps/db/src/logseq/db/frontend/inputs.cljs:143-162).
- :14d matches the deprecated regex (inputs.cljs:80) and is turned into :today-14d (inputs.cljs:19-23, 135-138), which gives a yyyymmdd int (inputs.cljs:121-125).
- :today gives date->int of today (inputs.cljs:100-101).
- :7d-after gives today+7.

The rules are conj'd onto the inputs (query_react.cljs:109-111).

CACHE KEY AND REACT: the key is [repo :custom query-string today-query? resolved-inputs] (query_react.cljs:112-115). react/q (react.cljs:128) returns the cached atom when one exists (react.cljs:142), so re-renders do not re-query. remove-q! never evicts today queries because (nth k 3) is today-query? (react.cljs:63-65). They stay cached for the session and only get a new key when the date changes. The first run waits 100 ms for built-ins (react.cljs:106-107), then db-async-util/<q (async/util.cljs:26-59) adds :db/id to the pull (async/util.cljs:18-19) and calls :thread-api/q. The worker runs a synchronous (apply d/q ...) on the full conn (db_worker.cljs:503-506), which blocks the worker.

RE-RUN: every worker->UI transaction goes through :db/sync-changes (handler/events.cljs:406-410) and then react/refresh! (modules/outliner/pipeline.cljs:93). From-disk transactions only re-render (pipeline.cljs:56-59). refresh-affected-queries! re-runs every :custom key regardless of the affected keys (react.cljs:184), unless it is collapsed (react.cljs:199-200). The run is queued until 1 s of input idle, retrying every 2 s (react.cljs:212-222; state.cljs:1781). So after every edit burst the NOW and NEXT queries run again in the worker. At 10k that is another 1.6-3.1 s stall per burst, on top of startup.

WHY IT SCALES (DataScript fork 3971e2d, query.cljc): clauses run strictly in order (-q, 817-819). A rule call is expanded against the outer context (solve-rule, 618-672). A pattern is looked up with lookup-pattern-db (408-418). It swaps a bound variable for its value only when that variable's relation has exactly one tuple (substitute-constant, 382-391). Otherwise the variable becomes nil and -search reads the whole attribute through AEVT: [_ a _ _] at db.cljc:748. It then hash-joins the result (collapse-rels, 448-456). Predicates only filter rows that are already bound (filter-by-pred). The comment "TODO optimize with bound attrs min/max" at query.cljc:409 marks that no range pushdown exists. Step by step, with g-10k counts (58 220 blocks, 10 000 journals, 3 383 task blocks, 77 NOW/DOING, 1 805 NOW/LATER/TODO):
(1) `(task ?h #{..})` or [?h :block/marker ?m] with ?h unbound reads the AEVT slice of :block/marker, i.e. all 3 383 task datoms. An index would not change this for [_ a _ _]. Then contains? leaves 77.
(2) [?h :block/page ?p]: ?h holds 77 tuples, more than one, so it reads the whole :block/page AEVT slice, about 58 000 datoms, one per block. On a lazily restored db (restore-data-from-addr, db_worker.cljs:215-240) this also loads every one of those leaves from SQLite.
(3) Built-in: [?p :block/journal-day ?d] reads the whole attribute, 10 000 datoms, and then the date predicates filter it.
(3') Johan's override: [?p :block/journal? true] becomes [_ a v _] on an attribute with no index and no datoms (db.cljc:744-745). The result is empty, the query stops early (query.cljc:808-809) and returns nothing.

Cost therefore follows tasks plus all blocks, not the 14-day window. g-real has 3 540 blocks and takes 0.15 s; g-10k has 58 220 blocks and takes 1.6-3.1 s, consistent with the :block/page scan dominating. That is an inference; a timer should confirm it. If a graph had exactly one matching task, step (2) would be a cheap lookup.

Note: the "DOING" query at state.cljs:413-425 belongs to db-default-config (DB graphs, property-based task rule). For file graphs the second built-in is "📅 NEXT" (state.cljs:395-406), which has the same shape. NOW is state.cljs:380-394.

changes.where: new ns logseq.db.file-based.journal-window: (plan query args rules) and (run db plan)
changes.change:
`plan` matches the query structurally; the order of :where clauses does not matter. It returns ::no-match unless all of these hold:
- :find is exactly [(pull ?h SEL)].
- :in is [$ ?lo ?hi] or [$ ?lo ?hi %], and ?lo/?hi are bound to integers.
- :where holds only:
  - a marker constraint on ?h: either `(task ?h #{str..})` together with the file `task` rule, identical to (rules/extract-rules file-rules/query-dsl-rules [:task]), or the pair [?h :block/marker ?m] [(contains? #{str..} ?m)];
  - [?h :block/page ?p];
  - [?p :block/journal-day ?d];
  - exactly one lower bound [(>= or > ?d ?lo)] and one upper bound [(<= or < ?d ?hi)];
  - zero or more page-constant clauses [?p ATTR CONST], where CONST is not a symbol.

`run` does bounded index walks:
- pages = (d/index-range db :block/journal-day lo hi), filtered with the exact original comparison functions (so > and < stay strict), then kept only if every page-constant clause is true: (seq (d/datoms db :eavt p ATTR CONST)).
- For each page, walk (d/datoms db :avet :block/page p). For each block, read (:v (first (d/datoms db :eavt e :block/marker))) and keep it when it is in the marker set.
- Return (map (fn [e] [(d/pull db SEL e)]) (distinct es)), the same shape d/q produces for a pull find (query.cljc:954-994).

:block/journal-day has AVET (file schema.cljs:82) and :block/page is an indexed ref (schema.cljs:26-27). The work is ≤15 journal datoms plus the blocks of those pages, independent of graph size. Follow the lazy-seq discipline of get-latest-journals (initial_data.cljs:258-280): realize the seq inside the call.

For file graphs only (skip when sqlite-util/db-based-graph? repo), try the fast path first: (let [[q & args] inputs, p (jw/plan q args)] (if (= p ::jw/no-match) (apply d/q q @conn args) (jw/run @conn p))). Log the time under a distinct tag (e.g. :q-journal-window) so the lsbench harness can tell it apart from the slow path. About 10 lines.

Add one rewrite: the clause [?x :block/journal? true] becomes [?x :block/type "journal"]. Legacy 0.10.x configs, including Johan's, the g-10k and g-real bench graphs, and likely anyone migrating from the old default template, then return real NOW/NEXT results instead of always nothing. The rewritten clause is a page-constant clause, so the fast path still matches it. The cache key k uses the original :query-string (query_custom.cljs:79-80) and is unaffected.

changes.where: node test next to the other deps/db tests

changes.change: No change needed. The matcher ignores clause order, so the built-ins get the fast path as they are. Do not reorder them as a standalone fix; that buys nothing in this engine (see current_behavior).

Until the compat rewrite ships, deleting the override block (or dropping the two [?p :block/journal? true] lines) makes the NOW and NEXT sections show results again. merge-configs then falls back to the built-ins, which are equivalent and use the task rule.

design.risks:
- **User-configured :default-queries:** config.edn replaces the built-in :journals vector wholesale (merge-configs, state.cljs:443-453). Because of that, fixing only the built-ins would not change Johan's or the bench graphs' cost at all. The structural matcher covers the built-ins, the legacy template, and user queries of the same shape, in any clause order. Any other shape falls back to d/q unchanged and stays unbounded. Examples: extra joins; `between` in DSL page queries (the DSL puts dates inside the rule call, not in :inputs; extending the matcher to it is possible later); [?p :block/journal? true] if the compat rewrite is not shipped (the fast path then returns empty exactly as today, just cheaply).
- **Advanced-query blocks inside pages with the same shape:** they also take the fast path. Results are identical by construction, and the differential test enforces that.
- **Rules:** the fast path must accept `task` only when the % argument carries exactly the file rule. A user rule named `task` falls back.
- **result-transform and the UI pipeline:** unchanged. The result shape is the same (a seq of [pulled-map]), so custom-query-result-transform (seq-flatten, with-pages, then the sci result-transform, query_react.cljs:35-62), filter-top-level-blocks and group-by-page behave as before.
- **Row order:** d/q returns rows in hash-set order. The fast path returns page-ascending, then entity order. NOW re-sorts by priority anyway. NEXT had arbitrary order before and becomes deterministic.
- **Pull selector:** the worker receives [* :db/id] from transform-pull-query. Use it verbatim with d/pull, which runs the same pull code as d/q.
- **React refresh keys:** unchanged, since the key is built on the UI before the worker call. Today queries stay cached forever (react.cljs:63-65) and re-run after every edit burst (react.cljs:184, 199-200). With the fast path that costs milliseconds, so no change is needed there. A later step could skip them when the transaction touches no journal page in the window.
- **DB graphs:** skipped explicitly; their task rule is property-based.
- **Engine-level alternative:** a generic fork change (per-value lookups for a small bound set in lookup-pattern-db, query.cljc:408-418, plus AVET range pushdown for the TODO at query.cljc:409, plus a planner or a rewrite that puts the date pattern first) is feasible. But the DataScript fork is a git dependency (deps.edn:7-8, deps/db/deps.edn:3), so Logsidian would have to own a fork. It changes execution for every datalog query in the app and needs thresholds and wide regression testing. That is effort L, better done as a separate ADR-003 step.
- **:db/index on :block/marker, rejected:**
  - It does not help: [?b :block/marker ?m] with ?m free is always the AEVT slice (db.cljc:748). AEVT already holds exactly the task blocks, and contains? is not pushed into the index. Only constant-value patterns use AVET (db.cljc:742-743). Even then, the following [?h :block/page ?p] still reads all 58k datoms.
  - First open costs one extra AVET datom per task block (3 383 at g-10k, about 6 % of blocks, small next to the full-text :block/title AVET). It also adds AVET leaves to every SQLite store, which is already 38-49 % of worker time on first open.
  - It is unsafe for existing graphs. On reopen, check-and-fix-schema! (worker/db/fix.cljs:6-23) transacts {:db/ident :block/marker :db/index true}. The fork's update-schema (db.cljc:1455-1470) only updates the schema map and never back-fills AVET (with-datom, db.cljc:1478-1490, indexes only new datoms). AVET lookups would then silently miss old tasks until the graph is re-indexed.
design.expected_gain: These figures are estimates, not measurements. Per run at g-10k, from 1.6-3.1 s of blocked worker (startup, plus once after every edit burst while today's journal is on screen) down to low single-digit milliseconds. The work becomes about 15 AVET datoms, about 6 blocks per page times 15 pages of AVET and EAVT seeks, and a pull of each match. At g-real, from 0.15 s to about 1 ms. NEXT gets the same bound (≤6 pages). Cost then follows only the blocks on the journal pages in the window, independent of the total number of tasks, blocks and journals. It also stops loading every :block/page and :block/marker AEVT leaf from SQLite on a lazily restored db. With the compat rewrite, Johan's NOW and NEXT sections show results again; they have been silently empty.
design.verification:
1. **Differential and edge-case tests:** the new node test in deps/db (see changes): fast path = d/q as sets on seeded random dbs, for built-in NOW and NEXT, the legacy override (raw and rewritten), month and year boundaries, > vs >=; ::no-match for near-miss shapes; the perf smoke test on a large db.
2. **Confirm the diagnosis before implementing (read-only REPL on the worker):** run the override query with the date clauses first and time it. It should stay slow. Then time the [?h :block/page ?p] step on its own. This confirms the :block/page scan dominates.
3. **Bench:** rerun the lsbench reopen on g-10k and g-real (bench/run-after.sh style). The `q pull ?h [*] :in $ ?start ?today` worker stall (2.0 + 1.6 s on reopen at 10k) should drop below the 50 ms log threshold and show up under the new fast-path tag. Then edit a block on today's journal, wait more than 1 s idle, and check that no worker stall of a second or more follows (the refresh re-run).
4. **Manual check:** open g-real with the compat rewrite. The NOW section lists the NOW/DOING tasks from the last 14 journal days (g-real has 5 NOW/DOING lines in total) and NEXT lists those from the coming 6 days. Toggle a task's marker and the section updates after idle. Compare against the same graph with the override removed from config.edn.

critique.problems:
The core idea is sound and the diagnosis is correct: the bench graphs run Johan's legacy override, which returns nothing and scans everything. The worker fast path is a good fix. But the design gets the refresh behaviour wrong, gets the cost model wrong, has a measurement trap, and bundles in an unrelated behaviour change.

Citations: I checked all of these against the worktree and the fork at ~/.gitlibs/libs/datascript/datascript/3971e2d4 and they are correct.
- state.cljs 380-394, 395-406, 443-453.
- page.cljs 239-258, 714-715.
- query.cljs 133-197, 170.
- result.cljs 19, 56-58.
- query_custom 27-67, 69-86.
- query_react 35-62, 64-93, 95-120.
- react.cljs 63-65, 106-107, 128, 142, 184, 199-200, 212-222.
- async/util 18-19, 26-59.
- db_worker 503-506.
- inputs.cljs 19-23, 80, 100-101, 121-125, 135-138, 143-162.
- schema.cljs 26-27, 47, 82; rules.cljc 30-33; block.cljs:360; initial_data 258-280; fix.cljs 6-23.
- Fork query.cljc 382-391, 408-418 (TODO at 409), 448-456, 618-672, 808-809, 817-819, 954-994.
- Fork db.cljc 742-748, 1455-1470, 1478-1490.
- Nothing in deps/ or src/main mentions :block/journal?. The g-10k and g-real :default-queries blocks are byte-identical to ~/OneDrive/Logseq/logseq/config.edn:142-172.

1. **Wrong claim about refresh.** The design says today queries "stay cached for the session" and that "from-disk transactions only re-render". That is false.
   - pipeline.cljs:56-59 calls (ui-handler/re-render-root!) with no arguments. At ui.cljs:84-88 the default is clear-query-state? true, which runs react/clear-query-state! (react.cljs:48-51) and resets both *query-state and *collapsed-queries.
   - So every from-disk transaction evicts NOW/NEXT and re-runs them on the next render. That covers external edits, OneDrive sync of Johan's graph, and the reconcile on reopen.
   - remove-q! (react.cljs:63-65) only protects against component unmount.
   - This is a second re-run trigger the design does not cover. It is probably also the source of the two NOW runs on reopen (2.0 + 1.6 s, adr003-step1-results.md:258-260).
   - Related:
     - Collapsing a section does not stop its first run. custom-query* calls run-custom-query unconditionally; only refreshes check the flag (react.cljs:199-200).
     - After midnight the previous day's today-query keys are never evicted, so every refresh keeps re-running them.

2. **The cost model is wrong: the time goes to cold SQLite restores, not the scan.** bench/step3-designs.json records, in one activity window, `q (pull ?h [* :db/id]) :in $ ?start ?today` at 2206 ms and then `q ... ?start ?next` at 63 ms, with 10 569 restores and 3968 ms spent restoring.
   - NEXT in the override does the same marker and :block/page AEVT scans. It took 63 ms because the nodes were already restored.
   - So a warm re-run after an edit burst costs about 60 ms at 10k, not 1.6-3.1 s.
   - The real stall is the first cold run, plus any run after the db value is rebuilt from storage.
   - The expected_gain ("once after every edit burst") and the re-run analysis in current_behavior overstate the problem.
   - Verification step 2 (time the [?h :block/page ?p] step on its own in a REPL) will mislead if run warm.
   - The fast path still fixes the cold case: it touches only a few dozen leaves. At about 0.37 ms per restore that is roughly 10-30 ms cold, not "low single-digit ms".

3. **Measurement trap.** perf-api! takes sync-ms at thread_api.cljc:83, before the result is written to transit at :92. d/q's pull is lazy (a `for` at query.cljc:960).
   - Existing q sync-ms numbers therefore exclude the pull.
   - A lazy `(map ...)` fast path would push its index walks, restores and pulls into the transit write, which blocks the worker just the same. It would show a sync-ms below 50 ms whether or not it is actually fast.
   - "Realize inside the call" is noted only as lazy-seq hygiene. It needs to be mandatory, and the bench comparison needs total-ms and restores per call.

4. **The compat rewrite is scope creep with side effects.** resolve-query runs on every advanced and react query in every page, not just :default-queries.
   - It rewrites only [?x :block/journal? true].
   - [?p :block/journal? false] and [?p :block/journal? ?j] stay silently broken, which is inconsistent.
   - It changes the meaning of the pattern inside not/or.
   - It turns user page queries that used to be cheap and empty into real result sets. Those queries do not match the fast path (they have extra joins), so they can bring back unbounded d/q scans and large renders: a new stall. It also silently overrides what the user wrote in config.
   - It is not needed for the performance fix: the fast path already handles the raw override cheaply.

5. **Matcher and test details.**
   - Page-constant clauses [?p ATTR CONST] on ref attributes, where CONST is an ident, lookup ref or eid: d/q resolves these through resolve-pattern-lookup-refs (query.cljc:393-406). I did not verify that d/datoms :eavt resolves ref values the same way (resolve-datom, db.cljc:1133).
   - plan's signature is inconsistent: `(plan query args rules)` in one place, `(jw/plan q args)` in the worker. The rules are simply the last arg when :in ends with %.
   - add-rules-to-query is private and lives in src/main/frontend/db/query_custom.cljs:27. A deps/db test cannot call it, so the differential test has to build % with rules/extract-rules.
   - deps/db/test/logseq/db has no file_based/ directory yet (fine to create).

6. **The journals-home stall does not fully go away.** The same render also mounts scheduled-and-deadlines (page.cljs:717-718). Its file-graph query (db/async.cljs:235-253) is `(or [?block :block/scheduled ?d] [?block :block/deadline ?d])` plus get-else per block: full scans on unindexed attributes, 410 ms at 10k according to step3-designs.json. Linked references (5.5 + 3.4 s) are a separate step. The design should not claim journals-home is fixed.

7. **Checked and fine:** result shape (a seq of [pulled-map]), result-transform, group-by-page, the cache key (built on :query-string before the worker call), the collapsed-state plumbing, skipping DB graphs, rejecting the :block/marker index, and the reasoning that reordering alone does not help.
critique.required_changes:
1. **Fix current_behavior and risks.**
   - State that re-render-root! clears the query cache: pipeline.cljs:56-59 → ui.cljs:84-88 → react.cljs:48-51.
   - As a result, NOW/NEXT re-run after every from-disk transaction (external edit, sync, reconcile) as well as after edit bursts.
   - Drop "stay cached for the session".
   - Add to verification: modify a journal file externally and confirm there is no second-long stall.

2. **Re-base the cost model on cold vs warm.**
   - Cite the 2206 ms NOW vs 63 ms NEXT in step3-designs.json.
   - Count restores per call. The *perf counters at db_worker.cljs:215-240 already exist; add a before/after delta to the fast-path log line.
   - Run the diagnosis on a freshly opened (cold) db, not a warm REPL.
   - Explain or measure why reopen shows two cold NOW runs (a cache clear via re-render-root!, or the db being rebuilt from storage).
   - Restate expected_gain: cold about 10-30 ms, warm about 1 ms; the edit-burst re-run was about 60 ms, not seconds.

3. **Make run strictly eager.** Return a vector, e.g. `(mapv (fn [e] [(d/pull db sel e)]) es)` after `(vec (distinct es))`. Compare fast path vs d/q in the bench using total-ms and restores, not only sync-ms (thread_api.cljc:83 vs :92).

4. **Split the :block/journal? compat rewrite into its own change,** or drop it. If it stays:
   - Handle true, false and variable forms consistently, or restrict it to exact detection of the legacy 0.10.x :default-queries template.
   - Leave page queries alone and inside not/or, don't rewrite.
   - Surface a one-time warning instead of silently changing semantics.
   - Until then, recommend the config fix to Johan (delete the override).

5. **Tighten the matcher.**
   - Accept page-constant clauses only on non-ref attributes with scalar constants, or resolve ref values with the same lookup-ref logic d/q uses. Add such a clause to the differential test.
   - Keep one API: `(plan query args)`, with rules taken from the last arg when :in ends with %.
   - In the deps/db test, build % with rules/extract-rules file-rules/query-dsl-rules [:task]; add-rules-to-query is private and lives in frontend.

6. **Narrow the success claims.** The journals-home render keeps the scheduled/deadlines scan (db/async.cljs:235-253, about 410 ms at 10k) and linked references. Either list them as out of scope with their numbers, or add the scheduled query as follow-up work in the same step.

7. **Optional:** evict previous-day today-query keys, since remove-q! (react.cljs:63-65) never does. Note that collapsing a section does not stop its first run.
